text:
**A. Murder.** Firing a gun at a player during a crowded game shows extreme, depraved-indifference recklessness toward human life, which is enough for malice even though the defendant didn't intend to kill. I don't agree with the team note: this goes well beyond ordinary criminal negligence, which would support only involuntary manslaughter. His intent to hit the opposing player also transfers to the teammate who was killed.

CONFIDENCE: 70
